title: A little saving, a little more possibility
excerpt: A simple way to start a savings habit, even when your income changes from month to month.
content:
You do not need a large amount to start a useful savings habit. Begin with an amount you can manage after food, rent, education and other essentials.

Choose a regular day to put money aside. If your income changes with the season, plan around the months that are easier and leave enough for the quieter ones.

Before opening an account, ask about the minimum balance, withdrawal conditions, fees and how interest is calculated. Take time to compare the answers.

This is an illustrative member education article for the Mero Sahakari demo. It is general information, not a personal financial recommendation.

title: What to bring to your first branch visit
excerpt: A short checklist to make your first conversation a little easier.
content:
For an introductory conversation, bring your questions and a clear idea of what you would like to do. You do not need to commit to a product on your first visit.

A real cooperative may ask for citizenship identification, recent photographs and address or income documents. Requirements vary by membership and service. Ask for the full checklist before sharing any documents.

Please do not upload identification or personal financial records to this sample website. No real branch appointments are arranged here.
imageAlt: Animated Nepali visitor carrying a document folder into a welcoming cooperative reception

title: Understanding your loan repayment
excerpt: Look beyond the monthly instalment and ask about the total cost.
content:
A monthly instalment is only one part of a borrowing decision. Ask about the annual interest rate, the way it is calculated, processing charges, late fees and early repayment conditions.

Write down the full amount you expect to repay and compare it with your household income. Leave room for unexpected expenses and quieter months.

The calculator on this demo uses illustrative rates and a standard reducing-balance formula. It does not check eligibility, include all fees or make a loan offer.
